evidence: Workbook (read via zipfile in memory): 'Quality Checks' A35 row 34, E - tests/, 'interactive_time_varying_and_viewport_behavior_is_exercised': 'If interactive/animated/responsive/themed, the judges actually click, wait, resize, or toggle - not score a still first paint.' The 'Internal Quality Checks' sheet row 35 has the same wording and no extra note; drawings contain no text and the workbook has no comment parts. Skill references/quality-checks.md:142-143 says to check that when a criterion concerns interaction, animation, theming, waits or responsiveness, the judge is told to click, wait, resize or toggle. WHAT IS TIME-VARYING OR INTERACTIVE HERE: instruction.md:3-5,7 and hireops_rules.md sections 3, 5 and 6 cover optimistic moves with rollback and focus, 15-second live updates that must leave the open card, note, focus and scroll alone, scroll-anchored loading of earlier messages, the new-message notice while scrolled up, live unread and seen marks, drafts and an ended session. Responsive and theme behaviour are explicitly out of scope: instruction.md:11 says 'A clear desktop workspace is what matters. We don't need theme switching or a special phone layout.' The task correctly drops the template's 390x844 rows (template polish/judge.toml responsive_layout, visual prompt.md:29 and visual_responsive_consistency), and visual/prompt.md:14 says 'Assess desktop craft at a conventional desktop viewport. No phone layout or theme switching is required.' No resize or toggle is owed. HOW THE JUDGES ARE TOLD TO ACT: functional/prompt.md:29 and polish/prompt.md:18 define one Timed observation protocol. The other person's step runs in an independent context inside one browser_run_code_unsafe action; t0 starts only after that step succeeds; the DOM is polled every 500 ms for 15000 ms 'or the longer watch a criterion names' without clicking, typing, scrolling, reloading or navigating; the action returns {triggerOk, met, ms}; a void attempt is defined and repeated at most twice, while a completed met:false is never repeated; facts are read after a 2000 ms settle; negatives are watched for the full 15 s and then confirmed in a fresh context; and inserted text gets a unique suffix. This matches Colderwater lessons 7 and 14. polish/prompt.md:14 says 'Each live row is one timed observation ... Read document.activeElement, field values and scroll offsets with page.evaluate.' Every live or time-varying requirement maps to concrete actions and waits: hro_two_people (functional/judge.toml:59-61) has Mei move a card and add one in her own context while Rafael's page is watched for 15 s. hro_messaging step 1 watches the reply arrive, and step 2 uses Shift+Enter, Enter, then reads the box, focus and the state after a reload. hro_long_thread (:140-141) has the judge type an unfinished reply, scroll the list up by wheel or scrollTop, run a timed send by Noor, then read place, notice, draft, activeElement and the unread count, go to the new message, then do a second timed send and reply while scrolled up. hro_unread_seen (:149-150) uses timed count, total and seen readings with a full-window negative for the Observer opening. hro_interview_places (:68-69) tries the full-Interview move through the UI and by replay, then reads the card's real place, the reason and document.activeElement. hro_moves (:41-42) reads the mover's page at the first look after the action. polish hro_pol_live_board (polish/judge.toml:52-53) has the judge make the board scroll, scroll partway, open details, click into the note and type, then run a remote move with a 60 s watch and read the details, note text, activeElement and scroll offset within 2 px, then type more to show it appends. hro_pol_live_thread (:61-62), hro_pol_earlier_place (:70-71, getBoundingClientRect before and after loading), hro_pol_failed_send (:79-80, a route abort or setOffline for one send) and hro_pol_session_resume (:88-89, sign out in a second tab, then Enter on the first) cover the rest. app_context.md:33-35 tells the judge to hold modifier keys during the click (lesson 8). Every prompt says to report every step and fails a skipped step (functional/prompt.md:31-33, polish/prompt.md:20-22, lesson 9). Gates and visual are correctly static first-render/read-only reviews, and none of them grades time-varying behaviour. COUNTERFACTUALS: a still-first-paint app with no live channel fails hro_two_people's live leg, hro_messaging leg 1, hro_long_thread's notice, hro_unread_seen and both polish live rows, because every one needs an observed change after a remote trigger. An app that live-updates by full re-render, losing the open card, note, focus or scroll, fails hro_pol_live_board, hro_pol_live_thread and hro_long_thread through the activeElement, value and scroll reads. An app that never rolls back fails hro_interview_places. A conforming SSE, polling or socket app is accepted (rules:129), with up to 15 s plus a 2 s settle, and 60 s for polish preservation, so speed is not double-graded. A UI that refuses before moving is accepted at :69. Residual (P3, no observed impact): hro_interview_places does not explicitly tell the judge to wait for the server's refusal before reading the rollback, so a judge that reads immediately after the click might see the optimistic state. Playwright MCP's click waits for the requests it triggered, and the server is local, which makes this unlikely. RUNTIME EVIDENCE: raw-evidence-index.json hashes were checked. All 8 artifact hashes match, and their matching_source_files hashes match the frozen solution bytes. qc/repairs/hireops-2026-10-03-workspace/results/workspace.json results 18 'live board: another person's move arrives without reload; open card, note draft and focus kept' (passed, arrival_ms 808), 19 (scroll-up arrival keeps draft, focus and scroll), 20 (seen and unread update live) and 22 (ended session) show the golden supports the exercised behaviours. That is scripted Playwright, not a configured judge run. No configured judge, Oracle or model run shows that the claude-code/glm judge actually performs these timed actions rather than over-passing (lesson 9). That required runtime evidence is missing, so risk=true.
suggested_fix: Optional hardening: in hro_interview_places, tell the judge to wait until the refusal is shown, or 2000 ms after the attempt, before reading E's place, the reason and the focus. Then get a configured judge run to show that the timed actions are really executed.
